questions.title: Shortest Path in Campus Grid
questions.prompt: Given a grid with open cells, walls, a start, and a target, return the fewest moves needed using four-direction movement. Return -1 if unreachable.

examples.input: grid with S at (0,0), T at (2,2), walls blocking some cells

constraints: Use BFS for unweighted shortest path.
hints: Use breadth-first search: check all cells 1 move away, then all cells 2 moves away, and so on.
Remember which cells you have already visited so you do not loop forever.
The first time you reach the target, the distance you stored is the shortest distance.

visualizer.title: Shortest Path: BFS visits by distance
visualizer.caption: Watch a queue-based search mark nodes so it does not walk in circles.

questions.title: Course Plan Topological Order
questions.prompt: Given courses and prerequisite pairs, return a valid order to take all courses, or an empty list if a cycle exists.
constraints: A course may have multiple prerequisites.
hints: Count how many prerequisites each course still has; that count is often called indegree.
Start with courses whose count is 0 because they can be taken right away.
Each time you place a course in the order, lower the count for courses that depended on it.

visualizer.title: Course Plan: graph order idea
visualizer.caption: Watch a graph traversal keep track of visited course nodes before choosing next steps.

questions.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Length
questions.prompt: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in a list of integers.
constraints: O(n log n) is ideal, O(n^2) is acceptable for discussion.
hints: A subsequence can skip items; it only has to keep the original order.
Keep a list where position i stores the smallest possible ending value for an increasing subsequence of length i + 1.
For each number, replace the first ending value that is greater than or equal to it; the list length is the answer.

questions.title: Edit Distance
questions.prompt: Return the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to convert one string into another.
constraints: Strings may be empty.
hints: Build a table where each cell stores the best answer for a smaller pair of prefixes.
Fill the first row and first column by counting how many inserts or deletes are needed for an empty string.
When characters match, copy the diagonal value; when they differ, add 1 to the cheapest insert, delete, or replace move.

questions.title: LRU Cache Simulation
questions.prompt: Simulate an LRU cache with capacity k over get and put commands. Return outputs for get commands.

examples.input: capacity=2, put 1 A, put 2 B, get 1, put 3 C, get 2

constraints: A simple ordered structure is fine for V1.
hints: You need fast lookup and recency order.
Accessing a key makes it most recent.
When capacity is exceeded, evict the least recent key.

questions.title: Median of Two Sorted Lists
questions.prompt: Given two sorted lists, return the median value of the combined sorted values.
constraints: A merge-based solution is acceptable for V1.
hints: You only need values near the middle.
A simple merge can stop after reaching the median index.
Handle odd and even total lengths separately.

questions.title: Word Ladder Steps
questions.prompt: Given a start word, end word, and dictionary, return the minimum one-letter transformations needed to reach the end word.
constraints: Every intermediate word must be in the dictionary.
hints: This is an unweighted shortest path.
Generate neighbors that differ by one letter.
Use BFS from the start word.

questions.title: Expression Evaluator
questions.prompt: Evaluate a string expression containing non-negative integers, +, -, *, /, and spaces. Use integer division toward zero.
constraints: No parentheses in this version.
hints: Multiplication and division have higher precedence.
One stack can hold signed terms.
Apply + and - by pushing terms, * and / by modifying the top term.

questions.title: Trie Prefix Counts
questions.prompt: Build a structure that supports inserting words and returning how many inserted words start with a prefix.

examples.input: insert cat, car, dog; count ca

constraints: Words are lowercase letters.
hints: A trie is a letter tree: each step follows one character of the word.
When inserting a word, increase a counter at each letter node you pass through.
To count a prefix, walk the prefix letters; if the path exists, return the counter at the last letter.

questions.title: Union Find Components
questions.prompt: Given n students and friendship pairs, return the number of connected friend groups.
constraints: Students are numbered 0 to n-1.
hints: Start by treating each student as their own group leader.
For each friendship pair, find both group leaders and connect the groups if they are different.
At the end, count how many different group leaders remain.

questions.title: Kth Largest Stream
questions.prompt: Process a stream of numbers and return the kth largest value after each insertion once at least k values exist.
constraints: Use a min-heap of size k conceptually.
hints: Keep only the k largest values seen so far.
The smallest of those k values is the kth largest overall.
When size exceeds k, remove the smallest.

questions.title: Decode Ways
questions.prompt: Given a string of digits, count how many ways it can be decoded where 1=A through 26=Z.
constraints: A leading zero cannot be decoded alone.
hints: Let dp[i] be ways to decode the first i characters.
A valid one-digit code adds dp[i-1].
A valid two-digit code from 10 to 26 adds dp[i-2].

questions.title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
questions.prompt: Given meeting intervals, return the minimum number of rooms needed so no meetings overlap in a room.
constraints: End equal to start can reuse a room.
hints: Sort starts and ends separately or use a heap.
A meeting starting before the earliest end needs a new room.
Otherwise reuse the room that ended.

questions.title: Clone Graph
questions.prompt: Given a graph node with neighbors, return a deep copy of the connected graph.
constraints: Node values are unique for this practice version.
hints: Use a map from original node to copied node.
DFS or BFS through neighbors.
Return existing copies when a node has already been cloned.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray With One Deletion
questions.prompt: Return the maximum subarray sum when you may delete at most one element.
constraints: Subarray must be non-empty.
hints: Track best sum ending here with no deletion.
Track best sum ending here with one deletion.
For one deletion, either delete current or extend a previous deleted state.

questions.title: Serialize Binary Tree
questions.prompt: Serialize a binary tree to a string and deserialize it back to the same shape.

examples.output: string that can rebuild the tree

constraints: Use null markers for missing children.
hints: Preorder traversal works well.
Write a marker for null children.
Deserialization consumes tokens in the same order.

visualizer.title: Serialize Tree: preorder visits root first
visualizer.caption: Watch a preorder traversal visit nodes in the same order serialization records them.

questions.title: Alien Dictionary Order
questions.prompt: Given words sorted by an unknown alphabet, return one possible character order, or an empty string if invalid.
constraints: Words contain lowercase letters.
hints: Find the first differing character between adjacent words.
That difference creates a directed edge.
Topologically sort the character graph.

questions.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
questions.prompt: Given a list of integers and a target k, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose values add up exactly to k.
constraints: Numbers may be negative.
hints: Use running prefix sums.
If current_sum - k appeared before, those prefixes form valid subarrays.
Count how many times each prefix sum has appeared.

questions.title: Maximal Square
questions.prompt: Given a binary matrix, return the area of the largest square containing only 1s.
constraints: Matrix may be empty.
hints: DP value is the largest square ending at a cell.
For a 1 cell, use 1 plus the minimum of top, left, and top-left.
Track the largest side length.

questions.title: Rate Limiter
questions.prompt: Design a function that returns true if a user action is allowed under at most k actions per rolling time window.
constraints: Timestamps are non-decreasing per user.
hints: Store recent timestamps per user.
Remove timestamps outside the window.
Allow only if the remaining count is below k.

questions.title: Top K Scores
questions.prompt: Given a list of scores and a number k, return the k highest scores from largest to smallest. Keep duplicate scores if they appear in the input.
constraints: 1 <= k <= length of list.
hints: You only need the k largest scores, not every score in a special structure.
For this practice version, sorting from largest to smallest is a clear first solution.
Return the first k sorted values, keeping duplicates if they are in the input.

questions.title: Any Word Has Prefix
questions.prompt: Return true if at least one word in the list starts with the given prefix. An empty prefix matches every word, so it returns true whenever the list has at least one word.
constraints: Words are lowercase strings.
An empty prefix matches every word; return true when the list is non-empty and false when it is empty.
hints: First handle the empty prefix case: it matches if the word list is not empty.
For a direct solution, check each word with a starts-with comparison.
Return true as soon as one word matches; if the loop ends, return false.

questions.title: Earliest Connected Time
questions.prompt: Given n students and events [time, a, b], return the earliest time when all students are connected. Return -1 if it never happens.
constraints: Events may be unsorted.
Students are numbered 0 to n-1.
hints: Sort the events by time so you process them in the order they happened.
Each event connects two student groups, so merge those groups when they are different.
Keep a group count; when it reaches 1, return the current event time.

questions.title: Tree Level Sums
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means no node. Return the sum of real node values at each level.
constraints: Use -1 only as the missing-node marker.
The input may be empty.
hints: Level-order means the root comes first, then all level 1 nodes, then all level 2 nodes.
Read the list in level sizes: 1 value, then 2 values, then 4 values, and so on.
For each level, add only real values and skip -1 because it means a missing node.

visualizer.title: Tree Level Sums: read one level at a time
visualizer.caption: Watch level-order traversal visit the tree row by row.

questions.title: Minimum Study Plan Cost
questions.prompt: A study plan has modules with different effort costs. Starting before the first module, you may move forward one or two modules at a time. Return the minimum total cost needed to finish after the last module.
constraints: The cost list may be empty.
Costs are non-negative integers.
hints: Let each position store the cheapest cost to stand there.
From each module, you can arrive from one step before or two steps before.
The answer is the cheaper cost to finish from the last one or two modules.

questions.title: Tree Right Side View
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means no node. Return the values visible when looking at the tree from the right side, top to bottom.
constraints: Use -1 only as the missing-node marker.
The input may be empty.
hints: Process the tree level by level.
For each level, keep the last real node value you see.
Append that last value to the answer for the right-side view.

visualizer.title: Right Side View: keep the last node per level
visualizer.caption: Watch level-order traversal remember the rightmost visible value.

questions.title: Redundant Friendship Edge
questions.prompt: Given n students and friendship pairs, return the first pair that would connect two students already in the same friend group. Return an empty list if no redundant pair exists.
constraints: Students are numbered 0 through n - 1.
Pairs are processed in input order.
hints: Use a disjoint-set structure to track friend groups.
Before connecting a pair, check whether both students already have the same group leader.
If they already match, that pair is redundant and should be returned immediately.

questions.title: Running Median Scores
questions.prompt: Given quiz scores arriving one at a time, return the lower median after each new score. The lower median is the middle value after sorting when the count is odd, or the lower of the two middle values when the count is even.
constraints: Scores are integers.
Return one median for each inserted score.
hints: A heap solution keeps smaller scores on one side and larger scores on the other.
For a clear first version, insert each score into a sorted list.
After each insert, the lower median is at index (length - 1) // 2.

questions.title: Lowest Common Ancestor Value
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means no node. Given two values that appear in the tree, return the value of their lowest common ancestor.
constraints: Tree values are unique except for -1 markers.
Both target values appear in the tree.
hints: In a level-order array, a node's parent index is (index - 1) // 2.
Find the array indexes for both target values.
Move the deeper index upward until both indexes match.

visualizer.title: LCA: climb parent links
visualizer.caption: Watch two nodes move up until they meet at a shared ancestor.

questions.title: Tree Path Sum Count
questions.prompt: A binary tree is stored as a level-order list where -1 means no node. Return how many root-to-leaf paths have values that add up to the target sum.
constraints: Use -1 only as the missing-node marker.
The input may be empty.
hints: Walk from the root while carrying the running sum.
A leaf has no real left or right child.
Count a path only when it ends at a leaf and the sum equals the target.

visualizer.title: Path Sum: carry state downward
visualizer.caption: Watch the running sum change along each root-to-leaf path.

questions.title: Linked List Merge Index
questions.prompt: Two linked lists share one nextIndexes array. Given two head indexes, return the first node index where the lists merge, or -1 if they never share a node.
constraints: Indexes are valid or -1.
Each list has no cycle.
Return the shared index, not the node value.
hints: Follow the first list and remember every index it visits.
Walk the second list from its head.
The first second-list index already seen from the first list is the merge point.

visualizer.title: Merge Index: remember one path
visualizer.caption: Watch one linked path mark visited indexes before the second path searches for overlap.

questions.title: Longest Subarray Sum K
questions.prompt: Given a list that may contain positive and negative values, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum equals k.
constraints: Numbers may be negative.
Return 0 when no subarray has sum k.
Use the earliest index for each prefix sum to get the longest length.
hints: Track a running prefix sum as you scan.
If current sum minus k was seen before, the values after that earlier index sum to k.
Store only the first index where each prefix sum appears.

questions.title: Maximum Pair XOR
questions.prompt: Given a list of non-negative integer access codes, return the largest xor value made by choosing two different codes.
constraints: Use two different indexes.
The list has at least two values.
A clear pair-check solution is acceptable for this practice version.
hints: XOR is large when bits differ in high-value positions.
Compare each pair for a direct first solution.
Keep the largest xor value found so far.

questions.title: Total Busy Minutes
questions.prompt: Given busy intervals [start, end], merge overlaps and return the total number of minutes covered by at least one interval.
constraints: Intervals may be unsorted.
Touching intervals like [1,3] and [3,5] count as one continuous busy block.
Each interval uses end minus start minutes.
hints: Sort intervals by start time.
Merge an interval when its start is before or equal to the current merged end.
Add the length of each merged busy block once.
